research_question: What is a wire transfer, how does it move money, and what protections and risks apply?

research_brief.purpose: Explain wire transfers for consumers using Federal Reserve and CFPB primary sources.
research_brief.audience: U.S. consumers and small-business owners sending or receiving wires.
research_brief.data_period: Fedwire statistics through September 2026; Federal Reserve and CFPB pages checked October 26, 2026.
research_brief.scope_limitations: U.S. focus; bank fees and cutoffs vary by institution and are not quoted.

queries.keyword: how does a wire transfer work
can a wire transfer be reversed

keyword_research.historical_note: Owner draft targeted 'wire transfer what is it' (Ubersuggest 9,900, SD 8). Primary switched to the grammatical 'what is a wire transfer' (8,100, SD 38) so it can appear naturally 8 times; owner phrase kept as secondary. Pending owner approval.

sources.title: What Is a Wire Transfer?
sources.scope: Wire transfer definition; domestic vs international
sources.verification_note: Quoted: 'a common way to electronically move money from one bank account to another'; domestic or between a U.S. and an international account.

sources.title: Fedwire Funds Service Business Continuity Guide
sources.verification_note: Quoted: RTGS 'owned and operated by the Federal Reserve Banks'; 'over 5,000 participants'; 'final and irrevocable once made'.

sources.title: Fedwire Funds Service Monthly Statistics, September 2026
sources.scope: Fedwire volume and value by month
sources.verification_note: Sept 2026 row: 19,786,425 transfers; $105,151,617M; average $5.31M; average daily $5,007,220M. 2025 monthly rows sum to 217,296,700 transfers and $1,148,267,267M (Fin Loom sum).

sources.title: Fedwire Funds Service
sources.verification_note: Quoted: 'mission-critical, same-day transactions'; listed uses (client payments, commercial settlement, federal tax payments, federal funds).

sources.title: Fedwire Funds Service and NSS Operating Hours
sources.verification_note: Quoted: business day begins 9:00 p.m. ET preceding calendar day, ends 7:00 p.m. ET; 6:45 p.m. ET core customer transfer cutoff.

sources.title: What Is a Remittance Transfer and What Are My Rights?
sources.verification_note: Quoted: disclosures list; up to 30 minutes to cancel unless picked up or deposited; 180 days to report errors from disclosed availability date; refund or resend.

statistics.claim: In September 2026 Fedwire processed 19,786,425 transfers worth about $105.15 trillion, averaging about $5.31 million, with average daily value about $5.01 trillion.
2025 Fedwire volume about 217.3 million transfers worth about $1.148 quadrillion.
statistics.method: Fin Loom sum of published monthly rows
statistics.limitations: Calculated, not a separately published annual total

content_gaps: Competitors rarely cite Fedwire's own description of RTGS and finality.
Few give current Fedwire volume data.
Few explain CFPB remittance rights (30-minute cancel, 180-day errors) versus domestic wire finality.
Few separate SWIFT messaging from settlement.
value_add: Fedwire facts quoted from Federal Reserve documentation, September 2026 statistics, a labeled 2025 annual sum, CFPB remittance rights, and a fraud-verification section.

claims.statement: The CFPB describes a wire transfer as a common way to electronically move money between bank accounts, domestic or international.
Fedwire is an RTGS system owned and operated by the Reserve Banks; payments are final and irrevocable once made.
